correctness.rationale: For each window length k the ordered histogram of counts by weight is a complete encoding of the multiset, and the first two moments are linear sums of those counts. The frozen certificate visits each fixed-width binary representation once and every start at every length. Independent exact bit-field window extraction over all 4094 words reproduces the profile counts and no split fibers through length ten. At eleven the two-moment and full profile counts are 1050 and 1052. The only splitting fibers are the two stated four-word sets, each split into two reversal pairs. In the order of the stated representatives the length-three cubic values are 49 and 43, and 50 and 56, so that cubic repairs both fibers. Reversal preserves the full histogram, and t³=t for weights 0,1 and t³=3t²−2t for weights 0,1,2, proving the short-window limitation. For n<3 there is no length-three information to add. None of this extrapolates past length eleven or asserts word reconstruction within a full-observation class.

value.rationale: Compression of a standard inverse-problem observable by its first two moments raises a distinct and motivated question: when does the compressed channel identify additional full profiles? The exact cutoff, concrete fibers and one shortest-window cubic repair specify a benchmark for using aggregated rather than individual reads, without conflating information loss with the already known failure to reconstruct a unique word.
